ai.description: This 50–70 mm frog is lime green with small white or yellow dorsal spots. It features large, fully webbed feet with orange-red membranes and distinct white fringes along the limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Zhangixalus burmanus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, thin white or pale line running along the outer edge of its forearm and tarsus.
ai.habitat: *Zhangixalus burmanus* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands, typically found at elevations between 800 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Burmese flying frog is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its large, webbed feet to glide between trees to forage for insects and escape potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Zhangixalus burmanus* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests containing approximately 100–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Zhangixalus burmanus* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Zhangixalus burmanus* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed croaks, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams or pools.
